1. Document the Dockerfile dependency requirements in @0xhoneyjar/events README — the package's postinstall hook needs bash, git, pnpm in the consumer's runtime image (or runtime image with same deps)
2. Consider committing the prebuilt dist OR shipping events as a real published npm package to skip the rebuild entirely (sovereignty trade — would conflict with the git-tarball-pinned pattern)

**Source**: BB review on PR #107 (https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/freeside-characters/pull/107#issuecomment-4551374705).

**File**: `packages/persona-engine/src/events/mint-event-subscriber.ts:172-174`

**Issue**: When an operator sets `NATS_TLS_CLIENT_CERT` but forgets `NATS_TLS_CLIENT_KEY` (or vice-versa), the throw says only "both must be set or both unset" — operator still has to inspect their env to figure out WHICH side is missing. With `JWKS_URL` set this lands as `process.exit(1)` in Railway logs, so the error message is the operator's ONLY signal.

**Fix**: Name the present + missing env vars explicitly. Example:
```
NATS_TLS_CLIENT_CERT is set but NATS_TLS_CLIENT_KEY is empty — both must be set together (set NATS_TLS_CLIENT_KEY) or both unset (also unset NATS_TLS_CLIENT_CERT)
```

**Severity**: MEDIUM (operator-confused-state, one-shot clarity matters in fail-fast contexts).

**Effort**: ~5 lines.

title: cubquests-interface prod deploy silently dead ~17d (tsx test polluted next build) — add deploy-failure alarm
description:
## Finding

`cubquests-interface` (Vercel project `faucet-interface`) production was **silently undeployable for ~17+ days**. Last successful prod deploy: ~35 days ago. Every deploy since errored at the `next build` type-check, so production stayed frozen on a stale build — and nobody was alerted (a silent failure, same class as the leaderboard frozen-index bug it was discovered alongside).

## Root cause

`tests/typescript/golden_resolution.ts` — a standalone `tsx` test runner (added by jani in cycle-099 Sprint 2D.c, loa #741) — imports a `.claude` generated file with an explicit `.ts` extension:
`from "../../.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/lib/model-resolver.generated.ts"`.
Valid under `tsx`; fatal for `next build`'s project-wide type-check (TS5097, `allowImportingTsExtensions` off, `tsconfig` includes `**/*.ts` with no `tests/` exclude). The build "Compiled successfully" then failed at "Checking validity of types".

## Fixed

`cubquests-interface#252` (merged): excluded `tests/typescript` from the app `tsconfig`. Production deploy went green again immediately (first successful prod deploy in ~17 days). This unblocked the leaderboard frozen-index repoint (`#253` + env flip).

## Follow-ups (the reason this is worth tracking, not just closing)

1. **Alarm on deploy failure.** A dead prod pipeline went unnoticed for 17+ days. There is no signal when Vercel prod builds start failing. Add a deploy-failure alert (Vercel → Slack/Discord, or a GH Action that fails loudly on a red prod deployment). This is the deploy-layer twin of the leaderboard freshness alarm shipped in #253.
2. **Framework test-infra shouldn't pollute consumer app builds.** loa-synced `.claude` test infra (`*.generated.ts` + tsx runners under `tests/typescript/`) gets swept into `next build` via `**/*.ts`. Consider: a dedicated tsconfig for tsx test scripts, or the loa framework keeping its test infra out of consumers' app-build include globs. Other loa-consuming interfaces likely share this latent risk.
3. **CI type-check parity.** Local `bun run typecheck` passed (likely via an `extends` base enabling `allowImportingTsExtensions`) while `next build`'s own type-check failed — the two type-checks disagree. Align them so local catches what the deploy build catches.

Refs: cubquests-interface#252, #253, ci-leaderboard-frozen-envio-index-zmc, loa#741.

title: Extract badge/leaderboard primitive into an API building (de-couple consumers from the raw index)
description:
## Context (why this exists)

The CubQuests Envio→Ponder cutover stranded `cubquests-interface` on a FROZEN badge index — board + per-user badges + on-chain quest verification all read a dead endpoint silently for ~14 months (see `cubquests-interface#251` + bead `ci-leaderboard-frozen-envio-index-zmc`).

Root-cause CLASS (not the instance): the badge/leaderboard **primitive is computed inside the interface**, which hardcodes a raw indexer GraphQL endpoint (`NEXT_PUBLIC_GRAPHQL_ENDPOINT`) shared across 6 consumers — the board, per-user badge view, quest verification (`Action`/`TrackedHolder`), and badge-claim status. One frozen/repointed/schema-drifted index silently breaks all of them. The isolation has leaked (OSTROM): a presentation surface owns an infrastructure relationship.

## Proposal (operator trajectory, 2026-06-01)

Extract the badge/leaderboard primitive into an **API building** that OWNS the index relationship and serves a typed, versioned leaderboard + per-wallet badge surface. Consumers read the building's API; nobody hardcodes a raw index endpoint again. Operator framing: "the core primitives that performed well here should be served by the API and able to be distributed anywhere."

Benefits:
- Repoints/cutovers happen ONCE, behind the building (this whole incident becomes impossible to repeat at the consumer layer).
- The primitive becomes distributable to any world/interface (factory model, ADR-008).
- Resolves the deferred "Hasura vs in-house Ponder GraphQL" question — the building picks its own read surface; consumers are insulated.

## Scope sketch (NOT committed — for the planning session)

- Decide the owner building: `activities-api` (the CubQuests→activities extraction target, already underway) vs a dedicated `freeside-badges` building.
- Define the belt: building consumes sonar's badge index (`belt-gateway`), publishes typed leaderboard + per-wallet badge + (optionally) quest-verification surfaces.
- Migrate cubquests-interface's 6 `NEXT_PUBLIC_GRAPHQL_ENDPOINT` consumers to the building API.
- Fold in the fail-loud + freshness pattern (from #251) at the building boundary, so staleness is observable once, centrally.

## Trigger to pick this up

After `#251` merges + the endpoint repoint stabilizes the immediate fix. This is the structural fix that prevents class recurrence; not urgent, but high-leverage for the factory trajectory.

Refs: `cubquests-interface#251`, `ci-leaderboard-frozen-envio-index-zmc`, ADR-008 (factory model), CubQuests→activities-api extraction.

description:
**Source**: BB review on PR #243 (https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa-freeside/pull/243#issuecomment-4551390001) — verified at freeside-sonar/src/lib/events-publisher.ts:102.

**Issue**: `@0xhoneyjar/events` substrate library defaults publishers to `InMemoryPrevHashStore`. Publisher restart resets the hash chain — next envelope's prev_hash anchors to genesis instead of the prior chain tip. Subscribers that recompute hash continuity would see a broken chain across restart boundaries.

**Impact**: Not blocking the v1 first-canary-post since sonar restarts are infrequent and consumers don't currently strict-verify chain continuity. But this is the substrate-side persistence gap that becomes load-bearing when:
- Sonar redeploys/restarts during high-volume periods (airdrop spikes)
- A second sonar replica boots and starts its own chain (no cross-instance coordination)
- Audit replay requires verifying chain integrity from genesis

**Fix shape**: Provide a `PrevHashStore` adapter backed by Redis (preferred for low-latency get/set per publisher_key) OR Postgres (preferred if event log already lives in Postgres). API contract is already at `packages/events/src/publisher.ts:64`:
```
export interface PrevHashStore {
  get(publisherKey: string): Promise<string | null>;
  set(publisherKey: string, hash: string): Promise<void>;
}
```

**Applies to ALL broker choices** — not Path-ε specific. The Synadia path (Path D) has the same hazard.

**Suggested release**: cluster-events-pillar v1.1 hardening — file in the cycle's NOTES.md as a v1.1 sprint candidate.

S305-T7: AUTH_BYPASS Code Safeguard
description:
Implement code-level AUTH_BYPASS protection: environment gate, startup check, build exclusion.

THREAT MODEL:
- Risk: AUTH_BYPASS=true in production allows unauthenticated API access
- Attack vectors: misconfigured env var, leaked .env, container env injection, Helm/Terraform variable
- Impact: Full API access without authentication
- Current state: AUTH_BYPASS env var honored without environment checks

SAFEGUARD DESIGN (defense in depth):
1. Positive allowlist: bypass ONLY when BOTH conditions met:
   a. NODE_ENV is explicitly 'development' or 'test' (not just !== 'production')
   b. No additional bypass-enabling env like FORCE_AUTH_BYPASS exists
2. Startup check: Server refuses to start if AUTH_BYPASS=true and NODE_ENV not in allowlist
3. Audit logging: Warning emitted at startup when bypass enabled
4. Build exclusion: Production Docker sets NODE_ENV=production
5. CI policy: lint rule flags AUTH_BYPASS in non-test code without NODE_ENV guard
6. Terraform/Docker manifests: CI check ensures AUTH_BYPASS never set in prod configs

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- AUTH_BYPASS only honored when NODE_ENV in ('development', 'test')
- Server refuses to start if AUTH_BYPASS=true and NODE_ENV not in allowlist
- Log warning emitted at startup when bypass enabled
- Production Docker build sets NODE_ENV=production
- CI check: grep for AUTH_BYPASS in docker-compose.prod.yml / terraform.tfvars returns 0

TESTING:
- AUTH_BYPASS=true NODE_ENV=production causes startup failure
- AUTH_BYPASS=true NODE_ENV=development works with warning log
- AUTH_BYPASS=true NODE_ENV=staging causes startup failure (not in allowlist)

EFFORT: Small (1-2 hours)
FR: FR-4 (SKP-005)

title: envio v2→v3 rpc syntax migration is silent-fail (deprecated rpc_config: blocks ignored, no warning)
description:
**Source**: Path ε HyperSync-strip session 2026-05-27. Discovered when PRs #26/#27/#28 to sonar-api appeared to succeed but the indexer kept hitting the revoked HyperSync token.

**The trap**: envio v3.0.0-alpha.17 silently ignores the v2 `rpc_config:` block syntax. When `rpc_config:` is the ONLY chain-source config, envio falls back to auto-discover-HyperSync. No warning, no error — just silent fallback.

**Working form (v3)**:
```yaml
- id: 80094
  start_block: 8221
  rpc:
    url: http://...
    for: sync
```

**Deprecated (silently ignored)**:
```yaml
- id: 80094
  start_block: 8221
  rpc_config:    # <-- ignored
    url: http://...
```

**Surface lesson**: when adding a new chain block to a v3 envio config, copy the syntax from an existing WORKING block in the same file — don't infer from old docs or memory. The config.mibera.yaml had one correct `rpc:` block at chain 80094 that demonstrated the v3 form; I missed it on the first pass.

**Fix landed**: sonar-api PR #29 (commit `05373ab7`) converted 7 deprecated blocks across config.yaml + config.mibera.yaml to the v3 form.

**For future cluster work**: this same trap will catch anyone authoring new envio configs by reference to v2 docs or older cluster code. Worth a CI lint that flags `rpc_config:` blocks in any file under `*envio*.yaml` shape — silent-fail config bugs are the worst kind.
